edition.name: Koetschau, Origenes Werke V: De Principiis (GCS 22, Leipzig: Hinrichs 1913) - Rufinus' Latin, with the Philocalia Greek for III.1 and IV.1-3; text from Internet Archive OCR (hOCR of scan 'origeneswerke05orig', gaps filled from second scan 'origeneswerke05orig_0')
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: 1. Erei δὲ ἐν τῷ κηρυγματι τῷ ἐχκλησιαστιχῷ περιέχεται ὁ περὶ χρίσεως δικαίας ϑεοῦ λόγος, ὁστις καὶ τοὺς &xovortac, πιστευϑεὶς εἶναι ἀληϑῆς, προχαλεῖται ἐπὶ τὸ καλῶς βιοῦν καὶ παντὶ τρόπῳ φεύγειν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, δηλονότι συγχατατιϑεμένους τῷ Ep ἡμῖν ἰδίᾳ oAlya διαλαβωμεν, ἀναγκαιοτάτου ὡς Evi μάλιστα προβλήματος. ἵνα δὲ νοήσωμεν τί τὸ αὐτεξούσιον, τὴν ἔννοιαν αὐτοῦ ἀναπτύξαι det, ἵνα ταύτης σαφηνισϑείσης ἀκριβῶς παρασταϑῇ τὸ ζητούμενον.
pass_a_gloss: He says in the ecclesiastical preaching that the word about the just anointing of God is contained, which, being believed to be true, also provokes the Gentiles to live well and to flee from sin in every way, clearly having sympathized with us, so that we might take for ourselves, as the most necessary problem. But in order that we might understand what the self-determined is, it is necessary to unfold the concept of it, so that with this having been clarified, what is being sought might be precisely presented.
pass_b_english: In the Church's preaching we find the message about God's just anointing, a message believed to be true that challenges even the Gentiles to live well and avoid sin in every way. This happens because the message has aligned itself with us, so that we might take up this matter as our most pressing problem. To grasp what it means to be self-determined, we must first unfold the concept itself; only then, once it is clear, can the question at hand be presented precisely.
notes: The Greek text 'ἰδίᾳ oAlya' is unclear and may be a scribal error.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both fail to translate the clause 'ἵνα δὲ νοήσωμεν τί τὸ αὐτεξούσιον' (in order that we might understand what the self-determined [is]) accurately regarding the scope of the necessity. The Greek 'ἵνα δὲ νοήσωμεν... ἵνα ταύτης σαφηνισϑείσης' uses two purpose clauses. Pass A translates the first 'ἵνα' as 'in order that we might understand', but then adds 'it is necessary to unfold' which is not explicitly in the Greek (the Greek uses 'det' which is OCR debris/uncertain, but the structure is 'in order that we might understand... in order that [after] this being clarified...'). More critically, Pass B omits the 'in order that' (ἵνα) structure for the first clause, rendering it as a simple infinitive 'To grasp...', losing the purpose-driven modality of the original sentence. Furthermore, Pass A's translation of 'ἰδίᾳ oAlya' as 'for ourselves' is a reasonable attempt at the garbled text, but Pass B omits the 'us'/personal aspect entirely ('aligned itself with us'), failing to capture the sense of the Greek 'ἡμῖν ἰδίᾳ' (to us privately/ourselves).
reasons: Pass B omits the purpose modality of the first 'ἵνα' clause: 'To grasp what it means to be self-determined' vs 'ἵνα δὲ νοήσωμεν τί τὸ αὐτεξούσιον' (in order that we might understand what the self-determined is).

review.notes: source: 'ἰδίᾳ oAlya' is unclear; English: 'to us privately oAlya'
reasons: The English translation includes 'to us privately oAlya' which does not match the Greek text 'ἰδίᾳ oAlya' and appears to be an unexplained addition.
uncertainties: The term 'ἰδίᾳ oAlya' is unclear and may be a scribal error.
